title: Homeostasis and endocrine communication
goal: Learning goalExplain homeostasis and compare endocrine communication with nervous-system communication.Before you beginCells function best within suitable ranges of temperature, water balance, nutrient supply and other internal conditions.

title: Hormones and their target cells
goal: Learning goalExplain receptor specificity and compare membrane-receptor signalling with intracellular hormone action.Before you beginA target cell is defined by its ability to recognize and respond to a particular hormone, not only by receiving blood.

title: Feedback and regulation
goal: Learning goalDistinguish negative and positive feedback and use feedback direction to predict changes in a hormone pathway.Before you beginName the variable being controlled. A response is not “negative” because it is harmful or “positive” because it is helpful.

title: The hypothalamus and pituitary
goal: Learning goalCompare the anterior and posterior pituitary and map major pituitary hormones to their targets.Before you beginTropic hormones act on endocrine glands. Other hormones can act directly on non-endocrine tissues.

title: Growth regulation
goal: Learning goalExplain hGH action and distinguish the effects of growth-hormone imbalance before and after growth plates close.Before you beginThe anterior pituitary produces hGH. A hormone can have direct effects and also act through another signalling molecule.

title: ADH and water balance
goal: Learning goalTrace ADH production, release and kidney action, then predict urine changes and distinguish causes of diabetes insipidus.Before you beginWater can move by osmosis. Reabsorption returns material from kidney tubules to the blood rather than sending it out as urine.

title: Thyroid hormones and metabolism
goal: Learning goalExplain thyroid-hormone action, trace its regulation, and distinguish primary thyroid failure from an upstream control problem.Before you beginA tropic hormone stimulates another endocrine gland. Negative feedback can reduce upstream secretion.

title: Calcium regulation: PTH and calcitonin
goal: Learning goalExplain the opposing effects of PTH and calcitonin and trace the main response to low blood calcium.Before you beginCalcium is needed for processes such as muscle contraction and neural signalling. Blood calcium and calcium stored in bone are different pools.

title: The rapid stress response
goal: Learning goalTrace sympathetic stimulation of the adrenal medulla and explain how epinephrine supports an immediate response.Before you beginThe sympathetic nervous system supports an action-ready response. Hormones can extend effects beyond individual neural connections.

title: Cortisol and longer-lasting stress responses
goal: Learning goalTrace the hypothalamus–pituitary–adrenal cortex pathway and explain cortisol’s metabolic and feedback effects.Before you beginACTH is an anterior-pituitary tropic hormone. The adrenal cortex produces steroid hormones.

title: Aldosterone, sodium and water
goal: Learning goalExplain aldosterone’s kidney effects, connect them to volume and pressure, and distinguish its control from cortisol control.Before you beginADH changes kidney water permeability. Sodium reabsorption and water permeability are connected but different processes.

title: Insulin, glucagon and blood glucose
goal: Learning goalExplain insulin and glucagon as antagonistic regulators, distinguish diabetes types, and interpret glucose patterns without overdiagnosing.Before you beginGlucose is a circulating fuel; glycogen is a storage polymer. The liver can change the amount of glucose entering the blood.

title: Integrated chapter review and final check
goal: Learning goalIntegrate hormone source, trigger, target, effect and feedback across the chapter.Before you beginA completed check records work. It does not prove that every written explanation is correct or replace your teacher’s assessment.
